title: RFC-001: JWT Token Rotation Strategy
content:
RFC-001: JWT Token Rotation Strategy

Summary

This RFC proposes a sliding-window refresh token rotation strategy for the Auth Service to balance security with user experience.

Motivation

Our current implementation issues long-lived access tokens (24h) with no rotation. This is a security risk: a stolen token is valid for up to 24 hours with no mechanism to revoke it short of rotating the signing key globally.

We need a strategy that:

  1. Limits the blast radius of a stolen token
  2. Does not force users to re-authenticate frequently
  3. Works correctly in concurrent tab/device scenarios

Detailed Design

Token Lifetimes

Token Type Lifetime Storage
Access token 15 minutes Memory only (no localStorage)
Refresh token 7 days HttpOnly Secure cookie

Rotation Protocol

  1. Client receives access_token (15m) + refresh_token (7d) on login
  2. When access_token expires, client calls POST /auth/refresh
  3. Server validates refresh_token, issues new access_token + new refresh_token
  4. Old refresh_token is immediately invalidated (single-use)
  5. If old refresh_token is used again → security event, invalidate entire session family

Concurrency Handling

A 30-second grace window allows concurrent requests to use the old refresh token. All requests within the grace window receive the same new token pair.

         t=0          t=15m          t=15m+30s
client:   ──── access ─────|── refresh ──|── invalid ──▶
server:                    │             │
                     new tokens      old token
                      issued         rejected

Drawbacks

  • Additional database write on every refresh (but amortized over 15m windows)
  • Grace window introduces a small reuse window (acceptable trade-off)

Alternatives

Long-lived access tokens (current): Simple but unacceptable security posture.

Short-lived access tokens without refresh: Forces frequent re-auth, bad UX.

Opaque tokens + central validation: Good security but adds latency on every request (cache helps but adds complexity).

Unresolved Questions

  • Should we implement token families for device tracking? (Proposed: v2)
  • Cross-device logout: should revoking one device revoke all? (Proposed: opt-in setting)
